title: Area and perimeter
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.geo.area.perimeter: Perimeter is the distance all the way around: add every side, including ones that aren't labelled.
hints.geo.area.rectangle: Area of a rectangle or parallelogram: base × height (the height goes straight up, not along a slanted side).
hints.geo.area.triangle: A triangle is half a rectangle: ½ × base × height. A trapezoid: the average of the two bases × height.
hints.geo.area.composite: Split the L-shape into rectangles, or take the missing corner away from the big rectangle.
hints.geo.area: Perimeter: around the edge. Area: squares inside. Triangles: half. L-shapes: split or subtract.

misconceptionMessages.geo.area-perimeter-swap: Area counts the squares inside (multiply); perimeter is the distance around the edge (add). Which does the question ask for?
misconceptionMessages.geo.perimeter-two-sides: A rectangle has four sides: two of each length. Add all four.
misconceptionMessages.geo.perimeter-missing-sides: An L-shape has six sides. Work out the two that aren't labelled and add all six.
misconceptionMessages.geo.parallelogram-side: Use the height (straight up, the dashed line), not the slanted side.
misconceptionMessages.geo.missing-subtracted: Area = width × length, so divide the area by the width to find the length.
misconceptionMessages.geo.triangle-no-half: A triangle is half a rectangle: don't forget the ½.
misconceptionMessages.geo.trapezoid-one-base: Use both bases: their average times the height.
misconceptionMessages.geo.composite-whole-rectangle: That's the whole rectangle. Take away the missing corner.
misconceptionMessages.geo.composite-labelled: Those two pieces overlap. Split the L into two rectangles that don't overlap.

sections.title: Perimeter
sections.objective: Find the distance around a shape.
explain: Perimeter is the distance around the outside, like a fence.

steps: An L-shape has six sides. Four are labelled.
The missing across side: 10 − 4 = 6 m. The missing up-and-down side: 8 − 3 = 5 m.

visual.caption: Tap through: find the missing sides, then add all six.

sections.key: Perimeter: add every side all the way around, including sides that aren't labelled.

sections.title: Rectangles and parallelograms
sections.objective: Find the area of rectangles and parallelograms.
explain: Area counts the unit squares that cover a shape.
A parallelogram rearranges into a rectangle: cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other.

steps: Area of a parallelogram: base × height.
The height is the dashed line, 4 cm (not the slanted 5 cm side).

sections.key: Area = base × height. For a parallelogram, the height goes straight up (the dashed line), not along the slanted side.

sections.title: Triangles and trapezoids
sections.objective: Find the area of triangles and trapezoids.
explain: Two copies of a triangle make a parallelogram, so a triangle is half of base × height.

steps: A triangle is half of a 10 by 6 rectangle.

sections.key: Triangle: ½ × base × height. Trapezoid: (top + bottom) ÷ 2 × height.

sections.title: L-shapes
sections.objective: Find the area of shapes made of rectangles.
explain: Break the shape into rectangles that don't overlap, or start with the big rectangle and take the missing corner away.

steps: The missing corner is 10 − 4 = 6 across and 8 − 3 = 5 down: 6 × 5 = 30 m².

sections.key: Big rectangle minus the missing corner (or split into two rectangles). Find missing sides by subtracting.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.key: Perimeter: add around the edge. Area: squares inside. Triangles: half. L-shapes: split or subtract.
